function_1: honey-bee visitation and legitimate flower access
eligibility_reason: The same honey-bee visitor can express legitimate or robbing behavior depending on cultivar floral morphology.
notes: Apis mellifera visits Duke legitimately; Duke has wider flowers and higher honey-bee visit rates than Bluecrop or Draper. All observed bumble-bee visits are legitimate.

function_1: honey-bee visitation and legitimate flower access
eligibility_reason: Cultivar morphology changes the behavioral role of the same honey-bee visitor guild.
notes: Apis mellifera is a frequent nectar robber on Bluecrop's long narrow flowers; all observed bumble-bee visits remain legitimate.

antagonist_guild: same visitor guild when nectar robbing
eligibility_reason: Corolla access changes visitor abundance and robbing behavior without a local plant-fitness endpoint for this manipulation.
notes: Normal flowers have visitor abundance 2.24 ± 1.45 per flower per 10 min; exact normal-treatment robbing percentage remains in Table 3 and is not inferred.

antagonist_guild: same visitor guild when nectar robbing
eligibility_reason: Corolla shortening reduces robbing but also impedes legitimate access when landing space is removed.
notes: Bees often attempt but fail to enter these short-tube flowers; both non-robbing and robbing visits occur.

antagonist_guild: same visitor guild when nectar robbing
eligibility_reason: Shortening the corolla while retaining landing space maintains overall visitor abundance close to control and lowers robbing.
notes: Visitor abundance is almost similar to normal flowers while robbing percentage is lower.

antagonist_guild: same visitor guild when nectar robbing
eligibility_reason: Resource availability shifts visitors between robbing and non-robbing behavior.
notes: At peak foraging time the lower-resource control has fewer visitors and much higher robbing than high-resource flowers.

antagonist_guild: same visitor guild when nectar robbing
eligibility_reason: Increasing nectar availability shifts the same visitor community toward non-robbing visitation.
notes: Robbing drops from 19.06 ± 5.72% in low-resource control flowers to 2.26 ± 3.68% in high-nectar high-pollen flowers.
